children: , Google's search, cloud and artificial-intelligence giant, fell approximately 2.3% to $341.15 Tuesday as investors absorbed another warning over the long-term risks of advanced AI. Former Google DeepMind safety researcher Bilal Chughtai, who left the company in July after working on artificial-general-intelligence safety and alignment, argued that the industry needs stronger coordination and a development pace society can realistically handle. His comments add pressure to the AI-safety debate, but they remain the assessment of a former employee rather than evidence that Alphabet is pulling back from AI investment or that DeepMind's existing systems have become uncontrollable.

Reuters reported that Google had not responded to its request for comment when the story was published. That distinction matters. Alphabet is simultaneously spending aggressively to push AI capabilities forward while managing the governance, safety and talent risks that come with that race. Chughtai's departure highlights the tension inside frontier-model development: the same companies trying to build more powerful systems also need researchers willing to challenge how quickly those systems should advance. For investors, the immediate question is less about one researcher's warning and more about whether safety concerns eventually translate into slower deployments, tighter regulation or higher development costs.

The financial engine remains huge. Alphabet generated $119.8 billion in second-quarter revenue, with Google Cloud sales surging 82% to $24.77 billion, meaning the cloud business contributed roughly 20.7% of total revenue as AI demand became increasingly important. Alphabet is also working with an investment budget of as much as $205 billion this year, leaving little room for execution missteps as the AI race intensifies. The valuation picture adds another layer: at $341.15, the shares sit 34.39% above the GuruFocus GF Value estimate of $253.85, an $87.30 premium. That suggests investors are already paying heavily for Alphabet's AI growth potential, making any sign of slower commercialization, rising safety costs or weaker returns on its enormous capital spending more important to the stock.

title: Alphabet Falls as a DeepMind Exit Reprices AI's Safety Race
